findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: evidence_verify_mpp, schema_validate_mpp, hash_compute_mpp · Private data: agent_wallet · Public sink: evidence_verify_mpp, schema_validate_mpp, hash_compute_mpp.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: evidence_verify_mpp, schema_validate_mpp, hash_compute_mpp · Private data: agent_wallet · Public sink: evidence_verify_mpp, schema_validate_mpp, hash_compute_mpp

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "evidence_verify" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Verify a structured assurance record and its referenced evidence against the frozen Blue Cap verification contract. Returns a deterministic machine-readable verification result with provenance and assurance information for automated governance and audit workflows." → after: "Verify supplied structured evidence and return a machine-readable verification result."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
